subject: Clearview Dx - Post-incident RCA, action owners & closure matrix
messages:
From: Tom Greene <t.greene@clearviewdx.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 500 spikes during morning batch window

Mina —

We saw a sustained latency spike across our nightly ingestion and a few 500s during the 06:00–07:30 ET window this morning. Errors were concentrated on requests that hit the reranking route. Our telemetry shows tail latency jumping from ~120ms to ~1.2s and a 4.6% error rate for that period. This is repeatedly impacting downstream processing and SLA reporting.

Can the Redwood team confirm root cause and estimated remediation timeline? We’re escalating internally and need a short summary for our execs by EOD.

Tom
Director of Platform
Clearview Diagnostics

Attachments: (logs reference) clearview_traces_20261001.tar.gz (listed)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Greene <t.greene@clearviewdx.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency + 500 spikes during morning batch window

Quick interim update:
- We see correlated KV cache misses on the dedicated pool serving Clearview (node group cview-prod-gpu). Prefix miss rate increased ~6x during the window; this explains higher token decoding time and backend queuing.
- A model rollout yesterday introduced a slightly different memory layout that increased cache churn under certain sequence-length distributions.
- Mitigation applied at 23:40 PT: rolled back to previous variant and increased cache capacity for the pool.

Current status: error rate dropped back under 0.5% and tail latency is returning to baseline, but we’re continuing a 48-hour monitoring window.

I’ll include logs and a timeline in the RCA doc.

— Dylan
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: inference_summary_2310.log

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greene <t.greene@clearviewdx.com>, Nora Patel <n.patel@clearviewdx.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Clearview Diagnostics — RCA, corrective actions, and closure matrix (v1)

Tom / Nora —

Attached: clearview_rca_v1.pdf, inference_logs_20261001.zip, and a closure matrix (CSV inside the Excel). Summary below.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: A recent model-variant rollout changed KV cache memory layout causing higher prefix eviction under Clearview’s sequence-length distribution, increasing decode latency and driving a small spike in 500s when pool queueing hit a threshold.
- What we did: immediate rollback to prior variant (23:40 PT), increased per-pool KV cache allocation, and tuned batch-size ceiling for the pool.
- Impact window: 06:00–07:25 ET (10/01/2026). Estimated affected requests: 1.8M tokens total; percentage of requests receiving >500ms latency peaked at ~7% for the pool.

Action matrix (owners & due dates):
1) Engineering: finalize a memory-layout gating test and prevent rollout on pools with non-conforming seq-dist. Owner: Jonas Weber. Due: 2026-10-09.
2) Runtime: implement soft-threshold fallback that reduces batch-size when tail-latency crosses X ms for >5 min. Owner: Dylan Brooks. Due: 2026-10-15.
3) Product/CS: update mutual action plan and SLA note for Clearview including a two-week monitoring period and a credit proposal. Owner: Mina Haddad. Due: 2026-10-06.
4) Platform: add pool-level KV cache headroom metric to Redwood Console dashboards for early alerting. Owner: Laura Bennett. Due: 2026-10-12.

Please find the detailed timeline, flamegraphs, and the log bundle in the attached files and the Drive link (above). We’ve opened JIRA INF-4521 to track the engineering work.

Next steps I’m proposing:
- Tomorrow (Mon) 10/04 at 10:00 PT we’ll run a short async review with Clearview to walk through RCA + credits proposal.
- Weekly follow-up until the actions are closed (I’ll own the cadence).

— Mina
Sr Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: clearview_rca_v1.pdf, inference_logs_20261001.zip, closure_matrix_v1.xlsx

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Clearview Diagnostics — Incident closure & executive summary (actions in progress)

Tom / Nora —

Final note for your execs: the immediate incident has been remediated and Clearview traffic is stable. Below is a short closure summary you can share internally.

Closure summary:
- Incident: KV cache eviction surge after model-variant rollout caused tail-latency and 500 spikes on the dedicated pool (Clearview).
- Remediation: rollback + cache headroom increase. Tail latency and error rate returned to baseline within ~45 minutes of mitigation.
- Ongoing work: engineering gating test (Jonas) and runtime soft-threshold fallback (Dylan). Both items have clear owners and tracked Jira INF-4521.

Credit proposal: as discussed in the call, we propose a 6% service credit for affected month; Mina will send the formal credit note and updated mutual action plan by 2026-10-06 (Owner: Mina).

Executive ask for Redwood: please reply-all to this thread with an approval for the credit proposal or any escalation to your procurement team. If you want a short readout to your CTO tomorrow, Dylan and Jonas are available.

Thanks again for working through this with us — we’ll keep the weekly cadence until all closure items are marked done.

— Mina
Sr Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: closure_matrix_v1.xlsx
